A3 PRODUCT AUTHORITY, QUOTED FROM contracts/release-contract/foundation-capabilities.json (which is PROHIBITED here, so the quotes are a read and not an edit). Twelve capabilities are declared. For each, whether its outcome_conditions.failure imports its observable_result items is stated, because that is what decides how much of observable_result is verdict-bearing.
(1) cap-repository-registration. user_action: 利用者は改善対象RepositoryをInstallationへ登録する。 observable_result: 登録後、Repositoryの識別情報、ApplicationのPreview/Stable状態、適用中の大原則とRepository固有ルール、Requirement Backlogの状態、利用可能なRunnerとAI資源、ループが実行可能かとその理由を確認できる。登録によって既存Application、認証情報、外部resourceは無断で変更されない。 success: 登録したRepositoryの識別情報とループ実行可否がowner UIに表示され、既存Application・認証情報・外部resourceが変更されていない failure: 登録が拒否される、または識別情報・実行可否のいずれかが表示されない external_dependencies.systems: GitHub, Git, Firestore, owner UI. providers: EMPTY. DOES THE FAILURE CONDITION IMPORT observable_result? NO -- it names exactly two of the six observables, 識別情報 and 実行可否. The other four are reported as measured presences or absences and do not change the verdict.

checks.name: ruling-cap-repository-registration-is-a-product-gap
argv: gh --version; gh auth status; git --version; python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('contracts/release-contract/foundation-capabilities.json'));[print(c['id'],c['external_dependencies']) for c in d['capabilities']]"
checks.summary:
THE RULING ON cap-repository-registration: IT IS A PRODUCT GAP M5 OWNS, NOT A DECLARATION-DERIVED DEFERRAL. Section 8.3 admits exactly two deferral grades and both are derived from the capability's OWN declaration: 'declares Google Cloud Run -> D1' and 'declares codex and opencode, unauthenticated on this machine -> M6'. Three independent measurements settle that neither is derivable here.
(1) The declaration. Read out of contracts/release-contract/foundation-capabilities.json: external_dependencies.systems is exactly [GitHub, Git, Firestore, owner UI] and external_dependencies.providers is EMPTY. No Google Cloud Run, no codex, no opencode. So neither deferral grade applies.
(2) Section 8.3's reverse constraint. The recorded reason for the earlier deferral was 'this task's declared side-effect surface excludes every forge and every remote' -- internal/api/live_dogfood_test.go's own log line at V2-022. That is a property of a DIFFERENT task's scope, i.e. the observation 'we could not reach it', which section 8.3 forbids as a source of deferral. A deferral must be derived from the capability's own declaration, never from the observation that the observer could not reach it.
(3) The systems it names are measurably present and usable on this machine, so there is no external-unavailable ground either. Measured in this worktree: `gh --version` reports 'gh version 2.92.0 (2026-04-28)' and resolves to /usr/bin/gh; `gh auth status` reports '✓ Logged in to github.com account wakuwaku3' with token scopes gist, project, read:org, repo, workflow; `git --version` reports 'git version 2.43.0' and resolves to /usr/bin/git. So 'could not' is false and only 'did not' is true, and only 'could not, by declaration' defers.
CONCLUSION: cap-repository-registration is one of the FIVE M5-owned capabilities, its check in this record is passed on measured grounds, and it is nowhere described as deferred. The deferral set stays exactly seven.

checks.name: the-five-seven-zero-split-re-derived
checks.summary:
THE 5/7/0 SPLIT, RE-DERIVED FROM THE DECLARATION FILE BY TWO INDEPENDENT PREDICATES rather than asserted.
PREDICATE 1 (membership by declared external system / provider), evaluated over contracts/release-contract/foundation-capabilities.json: the set whose external_dependencies.systems contains the literal 'Google Cloud Run' is exactly {cap-preview-operation, cap-stable-promotion, cap-loop-control, cap-loop-self-update}, size 4; the set whose external_dependencies.providers contains BOTH 'codex' and 'opencode' is exactly {cap-autonomous-resolution, cap-shared-resource-allocation, cap-provider-operation}, size 3; the two are disjoint; the complement is exactly {cap-repository-registration, cap-requirement-intake, cap-backlog-visibility, cap-human-input-request, cap-user-documentation}, size 5; 4+3+5 equals the declared capability count 12.
PREDICATE 2 (the reverse constraint, evaluated independently): for each of the five complement members, external_dependencies.systems contains no 'Google Cloud Run' AND external_dependencies.providers contains neither 'codex' nor 'opencode'. That is a separate quantification over a separate direction, so a capability cannot be silently moved between sets by editing one side only.
Both predicates are executed by internal/contracts/capability_declaration_test.go at every judging commit (G6a), together with a negative control over synthetic decoded input proving each assertion can fail. So the classification is re-executed by `go test ./internal/contracts` rather than argued inside this record, and growing the deferral set to eight would require either editing a prohibited declaration file or turning that test red.
HOW THE SPLIT IS EXPRESSED. contracts/schemas/evidence.json constrains checks[].status to the enum {passed, failed, skipped}; there is NO 'ineligible' member. So ineligible-by-declaration is recorded as `skipped`, one check per deferred capability, named exactly the capability id. That is not a convenience: G7 forbids counting a skipped test as a pass, which is exactly the property wanted -- a deferred capability must never be readable as an exercised one -- and internal/contracts/capability_evidence_test.go's reverse rule fires only on `passed`, so a skipped check correctly writes no evidence_ids and the capability keeps its empty array. Therefore: TWELVE capability-named checks, FIVE passed, SEVEN skipped, ZERO failed, and result passed. No skipped check may be read as a pass (G7); no deferred capability is called failed (section 8.3); and no M5-owned gap is called deferred (section 8.3's reverse constraint).
NO PRODUCT GAP BECAME A DEFERRAL. The five passed are cap-requirement-intake, cap-repository-registration, cap-backlog-visibility, cap-human-input-request and cap-user-documentation -- the same five the complement predicate produces, with no member added or removed. The seven skipped are the four Cloud Run declarers and the three codex-and-opencode declarers, and not one of them is an M5-owned gap.
